description: See how a stock split changes your share count and price while proving the total value stays exactly the same.

faqs.a: A split multiplies your shares and divides the price by the same factor — e.g. 4:1 turns 100 shares at $400 into 400 shares at $100. Total value is unchanged.
faqs.q: What happens in a stock split?

faqs.a: Yes. Reverse splits (e.g. 1:10) reduce share count and raise the price proportionally, also with no change in total value.
New shares = shares × (a ÷ b); new price = price × (b ÷ a). Before and after values are shown side by side to prove equality.
faqs.q: How are the new figures calculated?

howto: Enter the shares you own and the current price per share.
Pick the split ratio (e.g. 4:1, or 1:10 reverse).
Read your new share count, price and the unchanged value proof.
title: Stock Split Calculator
